toolIdentity.note: Whole-program Ghidra analysis was not repeated. Connection-specific native checks used bounded PE/Capstone inspection.

integration.method: Pre-launch LWScripts package augmentation followed by the official LastWarLauncher.exe; the game loads the bridge through its own Lua/xLua runtime.

transport.hostToGame: Authenticated per-user named pipe with framed JSON.
transport.luaAdapterBoundary: The managed in-game adapter relays framed named-pipe traffic to/from sequence-numbered JSON mailbox files consumed by Lua.
transport.activeFeatureTransport: FEATURE018 also uses exact-owner request/response files with 50 ms result polling.

cadenceAndLimits.managedPipeAdapterIdleLoop: 10 ms sleep when no frame/mailbox work is available
cadenceAndLimits.feature018ResponsePoll: 50 ms while a request is outstanding
cadenceAndLimits.interpretation: These are source-backed schedules and safety limits, not a measured CPU or RAM benchmark.

reconnect.transportReconnect: Same-session pipe transport can retry once per second, up to 90 attempts, after an authenticated session or initial host-unavailable state; authentication failures do not mint a new identity.
reconnect.gameRecovery: The native recovery monitor runs every 2 s and is enabled only when AutoReconnect and GameDesiredRunning are both true.

cleanup.behavior: Stop invalidates recovery, targets the captured owner, requires exact process/session evidence, cancels the launch binding, stops the lease, clears only identity-matching runtime files, and restores the preserved official Lua package only after owned-process shutdown is proven.

applicationBootstrap.classification: Confirmed application payload decryptor; not evidence of the game attachment method.
applicationBootstrap.behavior: Reads a 32-byte Local\LwTool_MasterKey mapping, reads LWAPPENC, removes the encrypted file, AES-GCM decrypts using the first 12 bytes as nonce, optionally zlib-decompresses, then compiles and executes core.py.

confirmedRendererBehavior: Launch action posts profile and menu_mode to native IPC.
Renderer does not invent connecting state.
Native/core status is described by the shipped JavaScript as realtime mmap-derived live PID plus ACT state.
The launch button has a 90 s UI fallback.

lastWarLauncherLiteral.interpretation: The resolved direct reference belongs to COM path selection, not a demonstrated game-launch or game-attachment call.

selectedImports.classification: present in outer executable; not linked by current evidence to the game launch chain
present in outer executable; not linked by current evidence to game communication

boundedNativeXrefs.directImportNegative: The outer executable does not directly import the common remote-memory injection APIs checked: OpenProcess, ReadProcessMemory, WriteProcessMemory, VirtualAllocEx, CreateRemoteThread, or NtWriteVirtualMemory. This does not constrain the encrypted Python core or dynamically resolved APIs.

actualGameConnection.reason: The authenticated core.py and matching ui.html payload are absent and the owner has never authenticated. The Launch Center mmap/ACT comments establish a status contract but do not reveal how the core launches, attaches to, injects into, communicates with, monitors, reconnects, or cleans up the game.
missingEvidence: A normal owner-authenticated core.py payload or a task-owned decrypted in-memory equivalent
Matching post-auth ui.html if connection controls are implemented there
A task-owned authenticated runtime observation linking game PID/session identity to concrete handles, mappings, pipes, sockets or loaded modules
Equivalent connected-idle CPU/RAM and start-to-connected timing

lastWarPluginUnauthenticatedWrapper.comparability: Not comparable to a connected game session.

connectedIdle.lwControl: NOT MEASURED in this research pass; no task-owned connected game was already running.
connectedIdle.lastWarPlugin: NOT MEASURABLE without authenticated core/game connection.

conclusionBoundary.reliability: LW-Control is substantially better evidenced and currently safer to retain. Competitor reliability is unknown, not demonstrated weaker.
conclusionBoundary.efficiency: No fair winner can be established. LW-Control has identifiable polling/file-I/O optimization headroom; LastWarPlugin connected-state cost is unavailable.
conclusionBoundary.attachment: LW-Control's method is known: in-process game scripting loaded through the official game runtime after pre-launch package augmentation. LastWarPlugin's actual game attachment method remains unknown.
conclusionBoundary.profileIsolation: LW-Control has proven retained per-profile controller/session identity but currently serializes real game ownership because the installed Lua package is shared per Windows user. LastWarPlugin advertises multi-open/sandbox concepts, but their isolation and cleanup implementation remain hidden in the missing core.
